recipes.name: Honey Hoisin Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 2 bunches green onions, cut into 2 inch pieces
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Whisk together the oyster sauce, Dijon mustard, hoisin sauce, ginger, honey, and soy sauce in a bowl until combined; stir in the green onions. Spread about 1/4 of the mixture into the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish. Arrange the pork chops over the sauce in a single layer, and pour the remaining sauce over the chops, covering them completely.

Bake in the preheated oven until the chops are no longer pink at the center and the juices run clear, 30 to 40 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 145 degrees F (63 degrees C). Baste once or twice while baking.
Drain the liquid in the baking dish into a saucepan. Turn on the oven's broiler, and place the chops underneath the broiler until caramelized and brown, 1 to 2 minutes.

Whisk the cornstarch with water in a small bowl, and whisk the mixture into the pan juices. Set the saucepan over medium heat, and bring the sauce to a simmer, whisking constantly until thickened, 1 to 2 minutes. Season to taste with salt and black pepper. Serve sauce with chops.

raw_recipe.headline: Honey Hoisin Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Savory-sweet pork chops, baked in an easy sauce with Asian-inspired ingredients like green onions, hoisin sauce and honey, make an easy weeknight main dish that's ready in just under an hour.

review.reviewBody: This was very good. Quick and easy for a week night dinner. I only made 1/2 the recipe and added about 1/2 tbsp of lemon juice to freshen it up a bit. I thought it could use a little kick though, maybe some siracha or hot chili sauce. Will definitely make this again. Thanks for the recipe, Denise!

I made per the recipe, except for the end-broiling of the meat. The sauce was very intense and a bit too salty. To broil the meat and make the sauce as per the recipe would, I think, made that intensity too much for my palate. Over all good. What would I change? Possible less hoisin sauce and increase the honey; or add a couple of Tbsp of jelly/preserves. Definitely make it again.

I used the recipe on a roast because I was too lazy to slice it up into chops before cooking and it was delicious. It just takes longer to cook, but using the same temperature reference it turned out moist. I cut back on the oyster sauce by half a tablespoon because I didn't want it to be too salty. I also didn't transfer the sauce into a saucepan before adding the cornstarch paste. I mixed it in the Pyrex in which I cooked the meat and then spooned it over the chops I cut after the roast was cooked. Worked out fine. I will make this again. Thanks for the recipe.

Against my better judgement, I made this recipe as written. The chops came out dry and tough. 400°F is too hot and 30-40 minutes is too long too cook chops. I always bake mine at 325-350° F. I like my pork with an internal temp of 145-150° F
 Also, because I was serving it over rice, I doubled the sauce..

I thought this was a nice change although my chops got a bit dry. (375 for 30 min) I browned my chops with s & p before going in the oven and perhaps this is why the sauce did not penetrate the meat. The hoisin added a nice smokey flavor while the ginger gave it a nice bite.

I made this with wild rice and asparagas and it was TASTY. I really enjoyed the consistancy of the sauce and ended up pouring it on my asparagas too. I did use fish sause instead of oyster sauce (although I dont really think it makes any difference) and added a touch of sriracha too. will definately make it again.
Great recipe, would recommend keeping an eagle eye on the temperature of the chops when they are in the oven as you may over cook them, as I did first time. Thanks for the recipe Chef.

Loved these chops! I followed the recipe exactly except I used chopped onions because I didn't have green onions. With the regular chopped onions, the sauce wasn't as thin & smooth but, we loved it that way. Very simple & easy, but very tasty! This will be in my recipe rotation for sure. Thanks to the author!
This was fantastic! Strongly recommend this recipe
I just doubled the recipe to make more sauce. Husband loved it!! But I don't think it makes 8 servings with reg recipe.
this receipe was a hit. tender snd so good. adding to my menu.
My family loved it it had great flavor and very tender. This is my families new favorite pork chops.
Very simple and easy for a weeknight meal. I served with yellow rice and broccoli. Very nice indeed..
This is a perfect way to cook pork chops. They were so moist and delish!! Def keeper!!
